witnesses.separates: the tiles of 3 sit at three corners of a rectangle of tiles: the concept bridges the two legs, and the outline of the tiles' bounding rectangle adds the two sides that meet at the missing corner
a lone tile of 1 sits between two tiles of 3 in tile row 0: the concept's bridge of 3 crosses it, and a bridge that a tile of another odd color blocks is not drawn

the four tiles of 3 form a square, so two of them lie on each tile diagonal: the cardinal bridges draw the square's sides, and bridges along the diagonals also paint the gap cells on its two diagonals

two tiles of 8 sit one row apart, so their interiors share one row and span different rows: the tile-level reading finds no tile row holding both and draws nothing, and the cell-level reading bridges the gap cells in the shared row

two tiles of 8 sit one row apart and share one interior row, and a lone tile of 1 sits between two tiles of 3 in tile row 0: the cell-level reading bridges 8 along the shared row, and the bridge of 3 crosses the 1 unless a tile of another odd color blocks it

two tiles of 8 sit one row apart and share one interior row, and two tiles of 3 lie on one tile diagonal: the cell-level reading bridges 8 along the shared row, and bridges along diagonals join the two tiles of 3

the middle tile of the tiling is missing, and the bridge of 1 along tile row 2 crosses the bridge of 3 along tile column 2 at the center of that empty place, a cell no tile of another odd color blocks: the cases that leave a cell of two claimants undefined give no grid, and a color drawn later covers the earlier one there

tiles of two odd colors alternate in one tile line three times: 1 and 3 in tile row 0, 1 and 4 in tile columns 0 and 4, and 4 and 8 in tile row 5, so the bridges of the two colors claim the gap cells where their spans overlap: the concept gives both colors there, a color drawn later covers the earlier one, and a bridge that a tile of another odd color blocks is not drawn
